# Estate survey and batch 1

| Kind | Now | Approx. size | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rules | 80 active (57 with obligations, 23 prod-only), T-81 to T-85 retired | 6 KB | High-water is T-85 |
| Obligations | 59 in `arc-next` (56 active, 1 split, 1 waived, 1 deferred) | 32 KB JSON, 57 KB rendered | Highest id is I-60 |
| Decisions | 39 lines | 2.7 KB | Highest id is C-40 |
| Debt | 15 open | 6.7 KB rendered | |

`arc-next` already omits I-54 and the C-39 line, so neither needs a decision.

**Witness problem.** `test/register.test.js` has three tests: `list`, `I-20` and `cancelled exports`. Every other active obligation has a "proves" judgment on an `I-n` test that doesn't exist, and the executor treats a missing test as not passing. So "Gives up: nothing" below means the rule still demands the property, not that a test covers it today. The next Phase 0 has to deal with this whatever you decide here.

I will save approved decisions to `../roadmap-inputs/drafts/compaction.md`, as you asked, rather than the skill's default path. Nothing has been recorded or edited yet.

## 1. retire T-8
- **Items:** T-8 and I-8, "The PortLink SOAP bridge retries failed deliveries every ten minutes."
- **Replacement:** none
- **Gives up:** the ten-minute delivery retry.
- **Why:** the bridge is gone. No commit has "PortLink" in `src` or `test`, and I-8 can't be witnessed.
  - Remove I-8 from the mapping and census, and trim the bridge sentence from the `register.md` prose.

## 2. resolve B-2
- **Items:** B-2, "Remove the retry queue in the PortLink SOAP bridge."
- **Replacement:** new ledger line `C-41 — The PortLink SOAP bridge and its retry queue were removed in arc-previous; B-2 has nothing left to remove.` The disposition is `{"type":"resolve","ruling":"C-41"}`.
- **Gives up:** nothing. No behavior is left unfixed.
- **Why:** the product overtook this debt.

## 3. retire T-33
- **Items:** T-33 and I-33, "Dispatch is allowed until 72 hours before the tide (working assumption P-1)."
- **Replacement:** none. T-72, "Dispatch is allowed until 48 hours before the tide.", stays as it is.
- **Gives up:** the 72-hour cutoff, which you already overruled when you answered P-1.
- **Why:** T-33 and T-72 contradict each other.
  - P-1 stays answered, and its `bears` moves from T-33 to T-72.
  - T-72 is prod-only, so this removes the only obligation on dispatch. The product has no dispatch code yet, so no test can cover the cutoff. I think that's acceptable for now, but it should be a deliberate choice.

## 4. merge T-27 into T-41
- **Items:** T-27 and I-27, "The export command refuses invalid dates." T-41 and I-41, "Every command refuses invalid dates before reading or writing records."
- **Replacement:** T-41 and I-41 keep their text. T-27 and I-27 are removed.
- **Gives up:** nothing. "Every command" includes export, and T-41 also sets the timing.
- **Why:** T-41 is strictly stronger.
  - The future I-41 witness must include an export case, or this becomes a loss.
  - The CLI has no date validation today, so T-41 is unmet with or without this merge.

## 5. merge T-65, T-66, T-67, T-68, T-69 and T-71 into T-41
- **Items:** "The `<command>` command validates dates before changing storage." for reserve, cancel, arrive, depart, list and inspect. All six are prod-only with no obligation.
- **Replacement:** T-41 keeps its text. The six rules and their census entries are removed.
- **Gives up:** nothing. Refusing before any read or write also covers refusing before a storage change, for all six commands.
- **Why:** six lines restate one rule.
  - I-41's witness then has to cover these six commands as well as export.

## 6. merge T-14 into T-3
- **Items:** T-3 and I-3, "A berth booking identifier is unique across the register." T-14 and I-14, "No two entries in the register have the same berth booking identifier."
- **Replacement:** T-3 and I-3 keep their text. T-14 and I-14 are removed.
- **Gives up:** nothing. The two rules say the same thing.
- **Why:** exact duplicate.
  - Point I-3's witness at test `I-20`, whose `/duplicate/` assertion covers this property, with a fresh proof judgment.

## 7. merge T-36 and T-37
- **Items:** T-36 and I-36, "The JSON export includes cancelled records." T-37 and I-37, "The CSV export includes cancelled records."
- **Replacement:** `T-86: The JSON and CSV exports include cancelled records.` with obligation I-61, witnessed by test `cancelled exports`.
- **Gives up:** nothing. The new rule names both formats, and the test asserts both.
- **Why:** one property, and one real test already proves both formats.

## 8. tighten T-49
- **Items:** T-49 and I-49, "In order to ensure that the operator can rely on the output when things go wrong, every failed command, without exception, prints its diagnostic to stderr rather than to stdout."
- **Replacement:** `T-49: Every failed command prints its diagnostic to stderr, not stdout.` I-49 takes the same text at rev 2 and needs a fresh proof judgment. `register.md` prose gains "Operators rely on command output when things go wrong, so failures stay off stdout."
- **Gives up:** nothing. "Every" carries "without exception", both the stderr and stdout requirements stay, and the reason moves to prose.
- **Why:** same demand in about a third of the words.

## 9. retire T-52
- **Items:** T-52, "Comment text is grammatical English." I-52, "One internal comment is grammatical English."
- **Replacement:** none
- **Gives up:** any requirement on comment grammar.
- **Why:** it serves neither V-1 nor V-2, and `src` has no comments for it to apply to.
  - I-52 is also narrower than its rule, so the rule and obligation already disagree.

## 10. retire T-70
- **Items:** T-70, "The welcome banner ends with a period." It is prod-only with no obligation.
- **Replacement:** none
- **Gives up:** the banner punctuation requirement.
- **Why:** the product has no welcome banner.

## What's next

Batch 2 covers T-62, T-63, C-23, C-30, C-38, C-12/C-17, the fold of C-4, and debt items B-6 and B-11. It also covers the index debt, where I expect to recommend closing most of it for a JSON-file register. Batch 3 covers the per-command rule and ledger families.

These items need care when we get to them:
- **T-5 and T-6:** they contradict the product. `list` and `export` exit 0 with no id, the `list` test depends on that, and the README documents it. I'll propose retiring them, not merging them.
- **Rule families:** each one skips certain commands, so "every command" would widen the demand. Replacements will name the commands explicitly.
- **T-54, T-55 and T-56:** these stay out of the sort merge. Merging would override the I-55 waiver and I-56 deferral, and it would pull T-54 back after I-54's retirement.
- **T-58:** I-58 is a split family with children I-59 and I-60, so it needs its own decision.
- **C-38:** `slips.json` cites it, so that citation has to go first.

I'm leaving these alone:
- **T-20, I-20 and C-34:** the integrity boundary, with recent findings F-1 and F-2 against it.
- **T-21:** it serves the current slice.
- **C-31 and C-32:** they are the authority for the I-55 waiver and I-56 deferral.
- **C-12:** `slips.json` cites it, so it can only change through the C-12/C-17 merge in batch 2.

One gap outside this review: every obligation serves V-1, and none cites V-2, your non-negotiable clause. T-3 and T-20 are the obvious candidates to serve it. That belongs in Phase 0.

Which of 1 to 10 do you approve? I recommend all ten.
reply:
1: approve
2: approve
3: approve
4: approve
5: reject. T-65, T-66, T-67, T-68, T-69 and T-71 stay.
6: approve
7: reject. T-36 and T-37 stay as they are.
8: approve with my wording only: `Every failed command prints its diagnostic to stderr, never stdout.` Play it back for explicit approval before recording.
9: reject as written. Retire I-52 only, which gives up the separate test demanding grammatical English in one internal comment. T-52 stays.
10: reject. T-70 stays.

I recorded 6 as K-13. Here is batch 3.

I ran the CLI against a temporary register for this batch. New obligation ids appear as `I-?` because Phase 0 assigns them. The merges name their commands explicitly, because each family skips some commands and "every command" would widen the demand.

You rejected the two merges of near-identical rules in batch 1, so 4, 7, 8, 9 and 10 may not appeal either. They are the biggest savings left. If you don't want per-command merges at all, reject those five and I won't propose the remaining families (T-25 to T-32, T-34 to T-40, the T-50 sort family, T-57 to T-64 and the C-n families).

## 1. resolve B-11
- **Items:** B-11, "Align the success message punctuation with the help footer."
- **Replacement:** new ledger line `C-43 — The CLI has no help footer and prints a bare record id on success, so B-11 has nothing to align.` The disposition is `{"type":"resolve","ruling":"C-43"}`.
- **Gives up:** nothing. No behavior is left unfixed.
- **Why:** one of the two things it aligns doesn't exist.

## 2. retire T-5
- **Items:** T-5 and I-5, "The list command rejects a missing record id with exit 2."
- **Replacement:** none
- **Gives up:** `list` rejecting a call with no id.
- **Why:** it contradicts the product. `list` takes no id and exits 0, the `list` test depends on that, and the README documents `node src/cli.js list`.

## 3. retire T-6
- **Items:** T-6 and I-6, "The export command rejects a missing record id with exit 2."
- **Replacement:** none
- **Gives up:** `export` rejecting a call with no id.
- **Why:** it contradicts the product. The first argument to `export` is the format, and with no argument it exits 0 and writes JSON.

## 4. merge T-1, T-2, T-4 and T-7
- **Items:** "The `<command>` command rejects a missing record id with exit 2." for reserve, cancel, depart and inspect, with I-1, I-2, I-4 and I-7.
- **Replacement:** `T-?: The reserve, cancel, depart and inspect commands reject a missing record id with exit 2.` with obligation I-?, whose witness must exercise all four commands.
- **Gives up:** nothing. All four commands stay named, and arrive and search aren't added.
- **Why:** four lines and four obligations state one rule.

## 5. retire T-9
- **Items:** T-9 and I-9, "The reserve command rejects an unknown record id without writing storage."
- **Replacement:** none
- **Gives up:** `reserve` rejecting an id the register doesn't hold.
- **Why:** it contradicts the product. A new id is how `reserve` creates a record, and my run of `reserve new1 one morning` exited 0 and wrote the file.

## 6. retire T-13
- **Items:** T-13 and I-13, "The list command rejects an unknown record id without writing storage."
- **Replacement:** none
- **Gives up:** `list` rejecting an unknown id. The no-write half is still met, because `list` never writes.
- **Why:** `list` ignores the argument. `list xyz` exits 0.

## 7. merge T-10, T-11, T-12, T-15 and T-16
- **Items:** "The `<command>` command rejects an unknown record id without writing storage." for cancel, arrive, depart, inspect and search, with I-10, I-11, I-12, I-15 and I-16.
- **Replacement:** `T-?: The cancel, arrive, depart, inspect and search commands reject an unknown record id without writing storage.` with obligation I-?, whose witness must exercise all five commands and check for no write.
- **Gives up:** nothing. All five commands and the no-write requirement stay.
- **Why:** five lines and five obligations state one rule.

## 8. merge T-17, T-18, T-19, T-22, T-23 and T-24
- **Items:** "The `<command>` command prints the record id on successful completion." for reserve, cancel, arrive, export, inspect and search, with I-17, I-18, I-19, I-22, I-23 and I-24.
- **Replacement:** `T-?: The reserve, cancel, arrive, export, inspect and search commands print the record id on successful completion.` with obligation I-?, whose witness must exercise all six commands.
- **Gives up:** nothing. All six commands stay named, and depart and list aren't added.
- **Why:** six lines and six obligations state one rule.
  - `export`, `inspect` and `search` print JSON rows containing the id, not the bare id. `export` with no records prints no id at all. The merge carries that question forward without settling it, so whoever writes the witness will have to.

## 9. merge T-42 to T-48
- **Items:** "The `<command>` command records the operator in the audit trail." for cancel, arrive, depart, list, export, inspect and search, with I-42 to I-48.
- **Replacement:** `T-?: The cancel, arrive, depart, list, export, inspect and search commands record the operator in the audit trail.` with obligation I-?, whose witness must exercise all seven commands.
- **Gives up:** nothing. All seven commands stay named, and reserve isn't added.
- **Why:** seven lines and seven obligations state one rule.
  - The product has no audit trail, so this is unmet with or without the merge.

## 10. merge T-73 to T-80
- **Items:** "The `<command>` command leaves the previous file intact when a write fails." for all eight commands. All are prod-only with no obligation.
- **Replacement:** `T-?: Every command leaves the previous file intact when a write fails.` Census state stays `prod-only`.
- **Gives up:** nothing today, because these rules cover exactly the eight commands in `src/cli.js`.
- **Why:** eight lines state one rule, and the write-then-rename in `src/cli.js` already meets it for the commands that write.
  - "Every command" also binds any command added later. That is a small widening, and T-41 already works this way. I recommend it.

Which of 1 to 10 do you approve? I recommend all ten. If you approve them all, rules drop by 25 lines before the new ones, leaving a net of 21 fewer.
